title: Which AI plan to choose?
author: Armored_Hoplite
selftext: Hello guys, I have been watching alot of AI videos lately and saw what are they capable of. I'm having this idea of starting to learn to code and for my first coding experience with AI i went with Roblox Studio route. (I will def try Godot and Unreal once I grasp the basics of programing). I want to rely on AI to write me code but also I want him to teach me as we go. I'm having trouble deciding whether I should go with 20€ GPT or Claude AI plan. I've seen fable5 is going away on 19th of July which is a bummer, since that was my favourite. Any of you have both and can give me some insights? Thank you.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body: 20 of anything isnt much claude no matter what your told esp fable. Fable 5 > what gpt has to offer as an objective statement by many .But gpt will give u more bang for ur buck alot more. It can teach u. And please do not pigeon hole yourself go out and use another engine unless u plan to build for roblox

replies.author: Armored_Hoplite
replies.body: Thank you! I know those plans are fairly limited when talking about amount of tokens and usage. I'm fairly new to prompting, learing about agents, sub agents and stuff so I will use pro subscription untill I grasp it better. Fable 5 is wild and I was so hyped when I saw it. I guess I will wait untill I learn more of this AI stuff and I might consider using more expensive plan.

replies.author: Armored_Hoplite
replies.body: Sorry I must ask one more question if you can bother to answer me. I imagined my workflow like this: I get the smarter subscription AI do game planing and mechanics implementation and all complex stuff and local LLM like qwen coder 7b or smth similar do all the code writing according to GPT/Claude commands. Is that doable, it should be, right?

replies.author: Accurate_Cable_1372
replies.body:
Local LLMs are cool but they are going to fuck up a lot still. What I would do is spend $40(lol) and get a $20 sub to ChatGPT and a $20 sub to Ollama. 

On Ollama you can use various open source models in the cloud. They’re going to be way smarter than if you ran them locally and you can get a lot of usage out of them.

So in theory you can have ChatGPT or Claude cook up plans and review, but you can use Ollama with a model like GLM-5.2 and have that do all of the implementation stuff.

That is more or less how I do it.

replies.author: Armored_Hoplite
replies.body: Thank you brother, I will definitely look into it.

replies.author: Accurate_Cable_1372
replies.body: No problem man, just hit me up if you have more questions

replies.author: Ok-Investment4414
replies.body:
accurate cable is right btw idk what people are doing with the off self (not trained on their own data) local models but they are gonna be a headache like accurate cable said. Gpt 5.6 high can get u way over 5k+ lines of clean functional code per week on that 20 sub. Claude 20 sub cannot. And the way u get that loc isn't codex its by the regular chat interface. Get the idea the product doc then chat out features , stack , how to implement etc. then get the larger picture followed by how to assemble the picture .

Image a large puzzle portrait of 4 people , to complete u can decide you will do 1 person at a time , but that's also difficult so u will start with 1 persons head , followed by their neck and shoulders, then you get to the arms . And now u find their right aright arm extends around the shoulders of person two, so now u also need to start working on person 2 shoulders etc. 

On budget that is the best way to do vibe coding. It gets the code u assemble and run test and give the results get feedback and how to fix. It's not perfect. 

Also learn while u go along. Even on a max 20x you will find out ai tends to fuck around and find out alot.

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: people can eat through 20 in any currency in a few prompts these days, I think codex seems like it does more, but I keep sticking with claude because it seems to get more done quicker and efficently. I would at least try the 20 codex plan and the 20 chatplan if you can't do the 100 plans from each other, that will let you figure out what works better. openai released there new models which I haven't tried but they should either be slighting behind or ahead of opus from what I read, some say the high end model is fable/mythos class but I've seen reports of people tearing that done. I have workflows in claude I can't move easier so I stay here, I have the $200USD plan for work, but I use the excess making games when I can.

replies.author: Armored_Hoplite
replies.body: Thanks! I was leaning towards the claude because, from what I understood, it has better  coding skills and integration into various IDE's such as Roblox Studio using MCP server but removal of Fable 5 made me question if I should begin with it or not. Many stated that Sonnet and Opus are not that good compared to Fable 5 (duh), but that GPT 5.6 is better than Sonnet and Opus so I started thinking I could try with GPT maybe. I do plan to take better payment plans in the future once I gain more knowledge.

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: opus is fine, people over sell fable, I've been doing stuff with games since sonnet 3.0. Its 100x easier now but opus can make the same games people are sharing, with a little more ffort.

replies.author: Accurate_Cable_1372
replies.body: They’re all pretty similar imo and ChatGPT can utilize the same MCPs that Claude does, nothing is LLM-specific. If I were you I’d just download the ChatGPT or Claude desktop apps and let them do their thing. Very doubtful anything you’re going to be doing is going to push the LLMs to their limit.

replies.author: Armored_Hoplite
replies.body: Yeah, all right. I'm fairly new and I won't be doing any complex coding and stuff like that. I will start with simpe games and mostly rely on AI to teach me what the code does etc...

comments.author: Just-Investigator-20
comments.body: I started using Claude at the beginning of the year with the $20 plan. After running out of credits four times a week, I upgraded to the $100 plan. It meets my needs now, so I haven't tried Codex.

replies.author: Armored_Hoplite
replies.body: Thanks! I'm fairly limited with my free time so I plan to learn to code like 2-3 hours daily. I can probably spare like 10 hours minimum weekly and 20 max. Do you think I would hit those too?

replies.author: Just-Investigator-20
replies.body: This usage depends not only on time, but also on your code content, problem difficulty, and task. My first Hit Limitation attempt involved converting my Godot project into a Phaser, which was extremely resource-intensive.

replies.author: MunchyCerealGuy
replies.body: Btw, definitely make sure to use the remote control features of Claude Code / Codex. I've been coding from my phone for the past few months. It makes it so much fun to be coding on the go and always have a little experimenting running the background of your day / sleep since you mentioned you have limited time
